mainTopic: More blemishes of a בכור: the Temple measuring cubits, missing testicles, leg and hoof defects, and אילא's list of blemishes.
overview: This amud opens in the middle of a משנה about the Temple's measuring cubits. In שושן הבירה there were two long cubits, one half an אצבע and one a full אצבע longer than משה's cubit. Workers were paid by the small measure and delivered work by the large one, so they would never commit מעילה. The גמרא explains that one long cubit was for silver and gold and the other for building. A second view links the ברייתא's אצבע to the flesh between a בכור's tail joints. A new משנה then deals with missing testicles, where רבי ישמעאל counts the sacs and רבי עקיבא presses to check. In the case of the hidden testicle, the גמרא shows that רבי יוחנן בן נורי's complaint was about eating קדשים outside. Further משניות and the גמרא on them cover leg and hoof blemishes, a broken leg bone, אילא's list with its three later-accepted additions, and the case of a lower jaw that sticks out.

steps.title: The two long cubits in שושן הבירה
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה describes two measuring cubits kept in שושן הבירה. One was half an אצבע longer than משה's cubit, and the other was a full אצבע longer.
steps.simpleTranslation: In שושן הבירה there were two measuring cubits, one in the northeast corner and one in the southeast corner. The northeast one was half a fingerbreadth longer than משה's cubit. The southeast one was half a fingerbreadth longer than the northeast one. So the southeast one was a full fingerbreadth longer than משה's cubit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is in the middle of quoting a משנה about the Temple's measuring sticks. Here the משנה describes two cubits kept in שושן הבירה and how much longer each one was than משה's cubit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three lengths here: משה's standard cubit, one that is half an אצבע longer, and one that is a full אצבע longer. The difference is counted in fingerbreadths, which is why this משנה was brought up while the גמרא was trying to pin down the size of an אצבע.

keyTerms.meaning: "Shushan the capital": a place on the Temple grounds named after the Persian capital, where these measuring cubits were kept
the standard cubit of משה (six טפחים)
fingerbreadth, a small unit of length

steps.confusionAlert: This section starts in the middle of a quote. The words "in שושן הבירה" continue a משנה that began before this section, which opened by saying there were two cubits there.

phrases.english: in Shushan the capital,
one in the northeast corner
and one in the southeast corner.
The one in the northeast corner

phrases.aramaic: הָיְתָה יְתֵירָה עַל שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה חֲצִי אֶצְבַּע,
phrases.english: was longer than Moses' cubit by half a fingerbreadth,
and the one in the southeast corner
was longer than it by half a fingerbreadth,
phrases.notes: "It" means the northeast cubit, not משה's cubit.

phrases.aramaic: נִמְצֵאת יְתֵירָה עַל שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה אֶצְבַּע.
phrases.english: so it turns out to be longer than Moses' cubit by a full fingerbreadth.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּשׁוּשַׁן הַבִּירָה, אַחַת עַל קֶרֶן מִזְרָחִית צְפוֹנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה that was being quoted before this section, as the source showing which אצבע the ברייתא means.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The northeast cubit was half an אצבע longer than משה's cubit, and the southeast cubit was a full אצבע longer.

steps.title: Why the Temple kept a large and a small cubit
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains the reason for different-sized cubits: workers took payment by the small measure and delivered work by the large one, so they would never come to מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why was there one large cubit and one small cubit? So that the craftsmen would take their pay by the small cubit and give back their work by the large cubit, so they would not come to misuse Temple property.
steps.whatsHappening: The quoted משנה continues and explains why the Temple needed a large cubit and a small cubit. It is a safety margin to protect the workers from מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Temple workers were paid from הקדש money. If they were paid for even slightly more work than they actually did, they would be using הקדש money they had not earned, which is מעילה. Paying by the small measure while requiring work by the large measure guarantees they always give back at least what they took.

keyTerms.meaning: craftsmen, artisans working in the Temple
misuse of הקדש (Temple property), a serious sin

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how careful the Temple system was about הקדש money. It was set up so that a worker could never accidentally walk away with Temple funds he had not earned.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָמָה הָיוּ אַחַת גְּדוֹלָה וְאַחַת קְטַנָּה?
phrases.english: And why was there one large and one small?
So that the craftsmen would take payment by the small one,
phrases.notes: Some versions say "when" (the word in round brackets), but the corrected wording in square brackets says "so that."

phrases.english: and give it back in work by the large one,
so that they would not come to misuse Temple property.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָמָה הָיוּ אַחַת גְּדוֹלָה וְאַחַת קְטַנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same quoted משנה and gives the reason for the different cubit sizes described in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Workers are paid by the smaller measure and deliver work by the larger one, to avoid מעילה.

steps.title: Why were two long cubits needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why there were two long cubits. One long cubit would have been enough to protect the workers.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need two?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא itself speaks. It asks why the Temple needed two different long cubits when one would have been enough for the safety margin. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the only goal is to make the workers deliver more than they are paid for, a single longer cubit would do the job. So having two different long cubits, one half an אצבע longer and one a full אצבע longer, needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: "why do I need": the גמרא's way of asking what something is for

phrases.english: Why do I need two?
phrases.notes: He means the two long cubits from step 1, not the large and small ones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the משנה just quoted: if the purpose is a safety margin, why are there two long cubits?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What was the purpose of having two different long cubits?

steps.title: One cubit for gold and silver, one for building
steps.stepSummary: Each long cubit had its own job. One was used for silver and gold work, and the other for building work.
steps.simpleTranslation: One was for silver and gold, and one was for building.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. The two long cubits were used for different kinds of work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Silver and gold are expensive, so the smaller margin (half an אצבע) was used for them, so the workers would not lose too much. Ordinary building materials are cheap, so the bigger margin (a full אצבע) was used for building. In both cases the workers always give back more than they take.
steps.whatToRemember: The Temple kept two long cubits: the half-אצבע one was used for silver and gold, and the full-אצבע one was used for building. Both make sure workers never take more than they earn.

phrases.english: One was for silver and gold,
phrases.notes: This is the shorter of the two long cubits, the one only half a fingerbreadth longer.

phrases.english: and one was for building.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each long cubit served a different kind of work: one for silver and gold, the other for building.

steps.title: Another view: the אצבע of flesh between the joints
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק (or רב הונא בר נתן) says the ברייתא's definition of an אצבע refers to our own משנה about a בכור with a full אצבע of flesh between one joint and the next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק, and some say רב הונא בר נתן, said: the ברייתא refers to what we learned in our משנה, where there is a full fingerbreadth of flesh between one joint and the next.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second answer to the earlier question of which אצבע the ברייתא was talking about. This view points to our own משנה about the blemishes of a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer connected the ברייתא to the Temple measuring cubits. This view connects it instead to the case in our משנה, where a gap of a full אצבע of flesh between joints counts as a blemish. On this view, that gap is measured as one quarter of an average person's טפח.

keyTerms.meaning: "and if you say": some say the statement belongs to a different rabbi
"to that which we learned": pointing to a known משנה
a joint or vertebra (here, of the tail)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two views on which אצבע the ברייתא defines: the extra length of the Temple measuring cubits, or the gap of flesh between the joints of a בכור in our משנה.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי תֵּימָא רַב הוּנָא בַּר נָתָן,
phrases.english: and some say Rav Huna bar Natan, said:
phrases.notes: The word "said" isn't written here, but the גמרא assumes it.

phrases.english: It refers to that which we learned:
phrases.notes: "It" is the ברייתא that defines an אצבע as a quarter of an average person's טפח.

phrases.english: where there is flesh between one joint and the next
a full fingerbreadth.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק, וְאִי תֵּימָא רַב הוּנָא בַּר נָתָן, לְאוֹתָהּ שֶׁשָּׁנִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of the Temple cubits and gives a different answer to the earlier question of which אצבע the ברייתא refers to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא's quarter-טפח אצבע refers to the full אצבע of flesh between the joints in the בכור blemish case of our משנה.

steps.title: The משנה lists missing testicles as a blemish
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states that a בכור with no testicles, or with only one testicle, has a blemish.
steps.simpleTranslation: MISHNA: If it has no testicles, or if it has only one testicle, it is a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It continues the list of blemishes that allow a בכור to be slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two cases are listed: no testicles at all, and only one testicle. Both count as a מום. The גמרא will soon ask why the first case is needed at all.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If it has no testicles,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא בֵּיצָה אַחַת.
phrases.english: or it has only one testicle [it is a blemish].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, separate from the measurement discussion in steps 1 through 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בכור with no testicles, or with only one, has a מום.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: go by the number of sacs
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל says that two sacs mean two testicles, and one sac means only one testicle.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל says: If it has two sacs, it has two testicles. If it does not have two sacs, it has only one testicle.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל gives a simple way to know how many testicles the animal has: count the sacs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Testicles are not always easy to feel. So רבי ישמעאל relies on what can be seen from outside, which is the sacs. Two sacs means no blemish, and one sac means it counts as having one testicle.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael says:
If it has two sacs,
it has two testicles;
if it does not have two sacs,
it has only one testicle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how to know which case of step 6 we are dealing with.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The number of sacs tells us the number of testicles.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: press the sac and see
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says to seat the animal on its rump and press the sac. If a testicle is there, it will come out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: One seats it on its rump and presses. If there is a testicle, it will eventually come out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives a physical test instead of counting sacs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא does not rely on the outside look of the sacs. He says to check directly by pressing. If no testicle comes out, we treat the animal as having only one.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
One seats it on its rump and presses,
if there is a testicle, it will eventually come out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי ישמעאל's method in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: We check by pressing, not by counting sacs.

steps.title: The case of the testicle stuck to the loins
steps.stepSummary: Someone pressed and nothing came out. After שחיטה, a testicle was found attached to the loins. רבי עקיבא permitted and רבי יוחנן בן נורי forbade.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a case where someone pressed and it did not come out. The animal was slaughtered, and the testicle was found attached to the loins. רבי עקיבא permitted it and רבי יוחנן בן נורי forbade it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells a real case that tests רבי עקיבא's method.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pressing showed no second testicle, so by רבי עקיבא's test the animal had a מום, and it was slaughtered. Afterward a hidden testicle was found. רבי עקיבא still permits it because the test is what counts. רבי יוחנן בן נורי forbids it, since the animal turned out to have two testicles after all.

keyTerms.meaning: The loins, the inner area near the kidneys

steps.confusionAlert: 'Permitted' here means the meat may be eaten as a blemished בכור. 'Forbade' means it was slaughtered without a real blemish, so it may not be eaten.

phrases.english: There was a case where one pressed and it did not come out,
it was slaughtered and found attached to the loins,
phrases.notes: The thing found is the second testicle, which had been hidden inside.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Akiva permitted
and Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri forbade.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A real case that tests רבי עקיבא's pressing method from step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא permits an animal that failed the pressing test even if a testicle was later found. רבי יוחנן בן נורי forbids it.

steps.title: Why mention 'no testicles' at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if even one missing testicle is a blemish, then obviously having none is a blemish. Why does the משנה need to say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: Now, if you said that having only one testicle is a blemish, is it necessary to say so when it has none at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first line of the משנה as unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists the bigger case (no testicles) and then the smaller case (one testicle). But if the smaller lack is already a blemish, the bigger lack obviously is too. So the first case seems to teach nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, since (introduces a 'this is obvious' argument)

phrases.english: GEMARA:

phrases.aramaic: הַשְׁתָּא אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא בֵּיצָה אַחַת
phrases.english: Now, if it has only one testicle
you said it is a blemish,
is it necessary to say so when it has none at all?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא בֵּיצָה אַחַת אָמְרַתְּ הָוֵי מוּמָא, אֵין לוֹ כְּלָל מִיבַּעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the first line of the משנה in step 6 and questions its wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's listing of 'no testicles' as a separate case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If one missing testicle is a blemish, then none at all is obviously a blemish, so the line is extra.

steps.title: Words are missing: the real cases are about sacs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is missing words. It really means two testicles in one sac, or two sacs with only one testicle.
steps.simpleTranslation: Something is missing, and this is what it teaches: If it does not have two testicles in two sacs but in one sac, or else it has two sacs and one testicle, this is a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by filling in words it says are missing from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'No testicles' really means not having two testicles in two separate sacs. Both testicles may sit in one sac, and that is a blemish even though both exist. The second case is two sacs that hold only one testicle. Now each case teaches something new.

keyTerms.meaning: Something is missing from the text
And this is what it teaches

steps.confusionAlert: After this answer, the first case is not an animal with zero testicles. It has two testicles that are both in one sac.

phrases.english: Something is missing, and this is what it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לוֹ שְׁתֵּי בֵּיצִים בִּשְׁתֵּי כִּיסִין
phrases.english: If it does not have two testicles in two sacs
but in one sac,

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי שְׁתֵּי כִּיסִין וּבֵיצָה אַחַת —
phrases.english: or else two sacs and one testicle,
this is a blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10 by reading missing words into the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: חסורי מיחסרא: filling in words missing from the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's first case means an animal with zero testicles, which would be obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first case is two testicles in one sac, and the second is two sacs with one testicle. Both are blemishes.

steps.title: The corrected משנה continues: רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: Still reading the corrected משנה: רבי ישמעאל says two sacs show two testicles and one sac counts as one testicle. רבי עקיבא says we don't assume, we press and check.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל says: If it has two sacs, it is known that it has two testicles. If it has only one sac, it is like one that has only one testicle. And רבי עקיבא comes to say: We do not say 'it is known.' Rather, one seats it on its rump and presses. If there is a testicle, it will eventually come out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps going with its corrected reading of the משנה and shows how the מחלוקת fits it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the new reading, רבי ישמעאל's words get sharper. Two sacs prove two testicles, so the 'two sacs, one testicle' case can't happen for him. One sac counts as one testicle even if two are inside. רבי עקיבא rejects the assumption from two sacs and requires pressing to check.

keyTerms.meaning: Is considered like, is similar to
And רבי עקיבא comes to say (introduces his disagreement)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל trusts the outside appearance: two sacs mean two testicles, one sac means one. רבי עקיבא says not to assume and to check by pressing.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael says:
If it has two sacs,
it is known that it has two testicles;
if it has only one sac,

phrases.aramaic: כְּמִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא בֵּיצָה אַחַת דָּמֵי,
phrases.english: it is like one that has only one testicle,
and Rabbi Akiva comes to say:
we do not say "it is known,"
rather, one seats it on its rump and presses,
if there is a testicle, it will eventually come out.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר: יֵשׁ לוֹ שְׁתֵּי כִּיסִים — בְּיָדוּעַ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ שְׁתֵּי בֵּיצִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the corrected reading started in step 11 and applies it to the opinions of steps 7 and 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Continuation of the corrected reading of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מחלוקת seemed to be only about counting sacs versus pressing for zero or one testicle.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי ישמעאל, two sacs prove two testicles and one sac counts as a blemish. רבי עקיבא denies 'it is known' and requires pressing.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's ברייתא: the case in פירן of בית מנחם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case and brings a ברייתא where רבי יוסי names the place it happened. The facts and the opinions are the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And there was a case where one pressed and it did not come out,' etc. It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יוסי said: There was a case in פירן of בית מנחם where one pressed and it did not come out. It was slaughtered and found attached to the loins. רבי עקיבא permitted it, and רבי יוחנן בן נורי forbade it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the last part of the משנה and brings a ברייתא that tells the same story in more detail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא adds the place where it happened, פירן of בית מנחם, and gives the story in רבי יוסי's name. The opinions match the משנה exactly, which confirms that the מחלוקת came from a real case.

keyTerms.meaning: The place where the case happened
Etc. (the quote continues as in the משנה)

steps.whatToRemember: Even when the hidden testicle was found after שחיטה, רבי עקיבא permitted the animal. For him the pressing test decides. רבי יוחנן בן נורי forbade it based on what was actually found.

phrases.english: "And there was a case where one pressed and it did not come out," etc.
It was taught in a baraita, Rabbi Yosei said:
There was a case in Piran of Beit Menachem,
where one pressed and it did not come out,
and it was slaughtered and found attached to the loins,
and Rabbi Akiva permitted,
and Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri forbade.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁמִּיעֵךְ וְלֹא יָצָא וְכוּ׳. תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the case from step 9 and adds details from a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The case happened in פירן of בית מנחם. רבי עקיבא permitted and רבי יוחנן בן נורי forbade.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא and רבי יוחנן בן נורי trade sharp words
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא accuses רבי יוחנן בן נורי of wasting Jewish money. רבי יוחנן בן נורי answers that רבי עקיבא is feeding people נבילות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to רבי יוחנן בן נורי: How long will you keep destroying the money of the Jewish people? רבי יוחנן בן נורי said to רבי עקיבא: How long will you keep feeding the Jewish people נבילות?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from step 13 continues. Each of the two תנאים attacks the practical result of the other's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא permits the animal because the pressing test showed no second testicle, so it counts as blemished even though one was found later; forbidding it, he says, wastes people's money. רבי יוחנן בן נורי forbids it because the animal really had two testicles and no blemish, so permitting it feeds people something forbidden. He calls this נבילות, a word the גמרא questions in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Destroying the money of the Jewish people
Animals that were not properly slaughtered

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri:

phrases.aramaic: עַד מָתַי אַתָּה מְכַלֶּה מָמוֹנָן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל!
phrases.english: Until when will you destroy the money of the Jewish people!

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri said to Rabbi Akiva:

phrases.aramaic: עַד מָתַי אַתָּה מַאֲכִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל נְבֵילוֹת!
phrases.english: Until when will you feed the Jewish people carcasses!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 13 with the closing exchange between the two תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא sees forbidding the animal as needless loss. רבי יוחנן בן נורי sees permitting it as feeding people something forbidden.

steps.title: But the animal was properly slaughtered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the word נבילות: the animal had a proper שחיטה, so how can it be called a נבילה?
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it slaughtered properly?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבי יוחנן בן נורי's word choice. The animal was properly slaughtered, so it cannot be a נבילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נבילה is an animal that died without a kosher שחיטה. Here the story clearly says that the animal was slaughtered. So the word נבילות does not fit the case.

phrases.english: Wasn't it properly slaughtered?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the word נבילות in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן בן נורי's word נבילות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A properly slaughtered animal can never be a נבילה.

steps.title: Maybe he meant טריפות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי יוחנן בן נורי really said טריפות, not נבילות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he said: טריפות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to fix the wording. Perhaps he said 'you are feeding them טריפות.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טריפה can be forbidden even after a kosher שחיטה. So this word seems to fit a slaughtered animal better than נבילה does.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals with a fatal defect, forbidden even after שחיטה

phrases.english: Rather: טריפות.
phrases.notes: The גמרא means: change his words to 'Until when will you feed the Jewish people טריפות?'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 by replacing נבילות with טריפות.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He said נבילות, which does not fit a slaughtered animal.

steps.title: But this has nothing to do with טריפות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the new wording: the question here is not about טריפות at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this is not a question of the prohibition of טריפות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own suggestion. A hidden testicle has nothing to do with the laws of טריפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is whether the animal has a blemish, a מום. It is not about whether the animal is a טריפה. So the word טריפות does not fit either, and another reading is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The prohibition of eating a טריפה

phrases.english: It is not a prohibition of טריפות!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer in step 16.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The case is about a blemish, not a טריפה, so the complaint cannot be about טריפות.

steps.title: He really meant eating holy animals outside
steps.stepSummary: The final reading: רבי יוחנן בן נורי complained that רבי עקיבא lets people eat קדשים outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he said: Until when will you feed the Jewish people קדשים outside?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct wording of רבי יוחנן בן נורי's complaint.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן נורי holds that this animal has no real blemish. That means it is still a holy unblemished offering. Eating it outside the proper place is forbidden, and that is exactly what רבי עקיבא's ruling allows.

keyTerms.meaning: Outside, away from the proper holy place

steps.whatToRemember: The real argument: רבי עקיבא sees this animal as blemished, so it may be eaten anywhere. רבי יוחנן בן נורי sees it as unblemished and still holy, so eating it outside is forbidden.

phrases.english: Rather: Until when will you feed
the Jewish people holy animals outside!
phrases.notes: Without a blemish the animal stays holy, so eating it like regular meat is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: עַד מָתַי אַתָּה מַאֲכִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל קָדָשִׁים בַּחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reading of step 16 with the final one.
steps.terutzMaskana: He said קדשים בחוץ, because to him the animal is not blemished.

steps.title: New משנה: blemishes of the legs and thighs
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists more blemishes: five legs, only three legs, closed hooves like a donkey's, a שחול and a כסול. It then defines שחול and כסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: An animal with five legs, or with only three, or whose hooves are closed like a donkey's, or a שחול or a כסול. What is a שחול? One whose thigh slipped out of place. And a כסול? One whose thighs are uneven, with one higher than the other.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It continues the list of blemishes that let a בכור be slaughtered and eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All of these are physical defects of the legs or thighs. The משנה also explains the two less familiar words, שחול and כסול.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal whose thigh slipped out of place
An animal with one thigh higher than the other

phrases.english: MISHNA: An animal with five legs,
or one that has only three,
or one whose hooves are closed like a donkey's,
or the שחול and the כסול.
What is a שחול? One whose thigh slipped out of place.
And a כסול? One that has one of its thighs higher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the testicle discussion to a new משנה about leg blemishes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Five legs, three legs, closed hooves, a dislocated thigh and uneven thighs are all blemishes.

steps.title: An extra or missing hind leg makes the animal a טריפה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says that the משנה means the front legs. With a hind leg, an extra or missing leg also makes the animal a טריפה, because an extra limb counts like a removed one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: The משנה taught this only when the missing or extra leg is a front leg. But with a hind leg, the animal is also a טריפה, because anything extra is considered like something removed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the new משנה. רב הונא limits the case of five or three legs to the front legs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a front leg, the extra or missing leg is only a blemish. For a hind leg it is worse: the animal is also a טריפה and cannot be eaten at all. The reason is the rule that an extra limb is treated as if the limb were missing.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this when (limits a ruling)
Anything extra is like something removed

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read רב הונא as saying the hind leg is not a blemish. It is still a blemish, but it is a טריפה too, so the animal cannot be eaten.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule 'anything extra is like something removed' is a well-known principle. It explains why having too much can be just as bad as having too little.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁחָסֵר וְיָתֵר בַּיָּד,
phrases.english: They taught this only when it was missing or extra on the front leg,
phrases.notes: In animals, יד means a front leg and רגל means a back leg.

phrases.english: but on the hind leg, it is also a טריפה,
because anything extra is like something removed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and limits the first case of the משנה in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Five or three legs is only a blemish when it involves a front leg. With a hind leg, the animal is also a טריפה, because an extra limb is like a removed limb.

steps.title: Round hooves count even if they are split
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the 'donkey hooves' blemish applies whenever the hooves are rounded, even if they are still split.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא says: Don't think it is a blemish only when the hooves are round and not split at all. Once they are round, it is a blemish even if they are split.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא explains the משנה's blemish of hooves 'closed like a donkey's.' He makes it broader than we might have thought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might think the hoof must be completely solid, like a real donkey's, to count. רב פפא says the round shape alone is enough, even if the hoof is still split. So the key sign is the round shape, not whether the hoof is split.

keyTerms.meaning: do not say (don't think it is only...)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa says:
Do not say it is only where they are round and not split,
phrases.notes: 'They' means the animal's hooves, from the משנה's case of hooves closed like a donkey's.

phrases.english: rather, once they are round,
even though they are split, it is a blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Like רב הונא in step 20, רב פפא explains another blemish from the משנה's list in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Round hooves are a blemish even when they are split.

steps.title: A ברייתא defines שחול and כסול
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that a שחול has a dislocated thigh, and a כסול has one hip bone out of place.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said 'the שחול and the כסול.' The Rabbis taught: What is a כסול and what is a שחול? A שחול is an animal whose thigh slipped out of place. A כסול has one leg bone sitting properly in the hip area and one leg bone sitting above it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes words from the משנה and brings a ברייתא that defines these two blemishes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both blemishes are about the hip and thigh. A שחול has a thigh joint that slipped out. A כסול is uneven: one side is in place and the other has slid up above the hip area.

keyTerms.meaning: an animal with a dislocated thigh
an animal with one hip bone out of place

phrases.english: The משנה said: "And the shaḥul and the kasul, etc."
The Rabbis taught:
Which is a kasul, and which is a shaḥul?
A shaḥul is one whose thigh slipped out of place.
A kasul is one whose one leg is inside the hip area, where it belongs,
and whose other leg is above the hip area.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַשָּׁחוּל וְהַכָּסוּל וְכוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵיזֶהוּ כָּסוּל וְאֵיזֶהוּ שָׁחוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the next words in the משנה from step 19 and backs up their meaning with a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שחול means a dislocated thigh. כסול means one hip bone is in place and the other is above it.

steps.title: A ברייתא defines the Torah's שרוע and קלוט
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that a שרוע has one thigh longer than the other, and a קלוט has closed hooves like a donkey or horse.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: What are the שרוע and the קלוט? A שרוע is an animal with one thigh that is too long. A קלוט is an animal whose hooves are closed, like a donkey's or a horse's.
steps.whatsHappening: A second ברייתא defines two blemishes that the Torah itself names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects the משנה's blemishes to the Torah's words. The קלוט is the same 'closed hooves like a donkey' blemish from the משנה, now tied to a word in the Torah. The שרוע is a thigh-length problem, close to the hip blemishes in step 22.

keyTerms.meaning: an animal with one limb too long

phrases.english: It was taught:
What are the saru'a and the kalut?
phrases.notes: These two words come from the פסוק: ויקרא 22:23.

phrases.english: A saru'a is one whose thigh became stretched out longer than the other.
A kalut is one whose feet are closed,
like those of a donkey and like those of a horse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second ברייתא that defines the Torah's terms, which are similar to the blemishes defined in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שרוע means one thigh is too long. קלוט means hooves are closed like a donkey's or a horse's.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'closed hooves' blemish in the משנה is the Torah's קלוט. Following רב פפא, round hooves count even if they are split.

steps.title: A broken leg bone, and אילא's list in יבנה
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה adds a broken leg bone as a blemish, even if it cannot be seen. It also says that the expert אילא listed these blemishes in יבנה and the Sages agreed with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If the bone of its foreleg or hind leg broke, it is a blemish, even if you can't see it. אילא listed these blemishes in יבנה, and the Sages agreed with him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It adds one more blemish and then tells us who first listed these blemishes and that the Sages accepted his list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most blemishes can be seen. Here a broken bone counts even when nothing shows from the outside. The historical note gives the list its authority: an expert named אילא presented it in יבנה, and the חכמים agreed.

keyTerms.meaning: an expert in blemishes of the בכור
the town where the Sages gathered after the חורבן

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ נִשְׁבַּר עֶצֶם יָדוֹ וְעֶצֶם רַגְלוֹ,
phrases.english: MISHNA: If the bone of its foreleg or the bone of its hind leg broke,
it is a blemish, even though it is not noticeable.
Ila listed these blemishes in Yavne,
and the Sages agreed with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ נִשְׁבַּר עֶצֶם יָדוֹ וְעֶצֶם רַגְלוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה that continues the list of blemishes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A broken leg bone is a blemish even if it cannot be seen. The list of blemishes was given by אילא and accepted by the Sages.

steps.title: אילא adds three blemishes the Sages had not heard of
steps.stepSummary: אילא added three more blemishes: a round human-like eye, a pig-like mouth, and losing most of the 'speaking' part of the tongue. The Sages said they had no tradition about these.
steps.simpleTranslation: He added three more, and they said to him: We have not heard of these. They are: an eyeball that is round like a person's, a mouth like a pig's, and losing most of the part of the tongue that a person uses for speaking.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists three extra blemishes from אילא. At first the Sages did not accept them, because they had no tradition about them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These three were different from the first list. The חכמים did not argue that they were wrong. They only said they had never heard them. The next step tells how this was settled.

keyTerms.meaning: we have not heard (we have no tradition about it)

steps.confusionAlert: 'We have not heard these' does not mean the Sages said these are not blemishes. It only means they had no tradition about them yet.

phrases.english: And he added three more,

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: לֹא שָׁמַעְנוּ אֶת אֵלּוּ.
phrases.english: and they said to him: We have not heard of these.
They are: an animal whose eyeball is round like a person's,
or whose mouth looks like a pig's,
or where most of the 'speaking' part of its tongue was removed.
phrases.notes: Animals don't talk. He means the part of the tongue that matches the part a person uses to speak.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד שְׁלֹשָׁה הוֹסִיף, אָמְרוּ לוֹ: לֹא שָׁמַעְנוּ אֶת אֵלּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of אילא: after the accepted list, he adds three more, and the Sages hold back.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אילא added three blemishes. The Sages of his time had no tradition about them.

steps.title: A later court accepts the three blemishes
steps.stepSummary: The בית דין of the next generation ruled that each of אילא's three extra blemishes is a real blemish.
steps.simpleTranslation: The court that came after them said: This is a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends the story. A later בית דין accepted אילא's three blemishes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What the earlier Sages left open, the next court decided. So in the end, all three of אילא's additions are real blemishes that allow a בכור to be slaughtered.

keyTerms.meaning: the court that came after them

steps.whatToRemember: All of אילא's blemishes were accepted in the end: the first list right away in יבנה, and the three extra ones by the court of the next generation.

phrases.english: The court that came after them said:
This is a blemish.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל אַחֲרֵיהֶן אָמְרוּ: הֲרֵי זֶה מוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the open question from step 25.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A round human-like eye, a pig-like mouth, and losing most of the 'speaking' part of the tongue are all blemishes.

steps.title: How can an unseen break be a blemish?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the משנה's rule that a broken leg bone counts as a blemish even if it cannot be seen.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: If it cannot be seen, is it really a blemish?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and challenges the משנה from step 24. A blemish is supposed to be visible, so how can a hidden break count?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blemishes that allow a בכור to be slaughtered are normally on parts of the body you can see. The משנה said a broken leg bone is a blemish 'even though it is not seen'. That seems to clash with this basic rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains and questions the משנה
It cannot be seen or noticed

phrases.english: GEMARA: It is not noticeable,
phrases.notes: This goes back to the broken leg bone in the משנה from step 24.

phrases.english: is it a blemish?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵינוֹ נִיכָּר, מִי קָא הָוֵי מוּמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה, going back to the broken-leg blemish from step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that a broken leg bone is a blemish even though it cannot be seen.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A blemish has to be visible, so something that cannot be seen should not count.

steps.title: You can tell from how the animal walks
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the leg looks normal, but the break shows when the animal moves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It cannot be seen by itself, but it can be seen through its work.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question. The leg looks normal, but you can see the problem when the animal walks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Not seen' in the משנה only means the leg's shape does not look different. The break still shows when the animal uses the leg, so it does count as a visible blemish.

keyTerms.meaning: By itself, from just looking at it
Through its work, meaning when the animal moves

steps.whatToRemember: A broken leg bone is a blemish because you can see it in the animal's walk, even if the leg looks normal.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
It is not noticeable on its own account,
but it is noticeable on account of its work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Not seen' means the blemish cannot be noticed at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Not seen' only means the leg's shape looks normal. The blemish shows in how the animal walks.

steps.title: Is a round eye unusual for animals?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws an idea from אילא's list: a round, human-like eye must not be normal for animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'These blemishes he counted,' and so on. Does this mean that it is not their normal way?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה about אילא and draws a conclusion from it. This sets up a contradiction that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a round, human-like eye counts as a blemish, the משנה must think animals do not normally have eyes like that. The גמרא states this idea so it can test it against another source.

keyTerms.meaning: And so on, meaning the quote continues

phrases.english: These blemishes he counted, and so on.
phrases.notes: This is the משנה about אילא from steps 24–25, and the point here is the round, human-like eye.

phrases.english: Is this to say that this is not its normal way?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: אילא's round-eye blemish.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the משנה assumes that a round, human-like eye is not normal for animals.

steps.title: A משנה in נדה suggests animals have round eyes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה in נדה and רבי יוחנן's reason for רבי מאיר, which says animals' eyes are round like a person's.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised a contradiction: A woman who miscarries something shaped like a domestic animal, a wild animal, or a bird, whether kosher or not kosher: if it is male, she keeps the days of a boy. If it is female, she keeps the days of a girl. If no one knows, she keeps the days of both a boy and a girl. This is the opinion of רבי מאיר. רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: What is רבי מאיר's reason? Because its eyeball is round like a person's!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source that seems to contradict the last step. רבי יוחנן explains that רבי מאיר treats an animal-shaped miscarriage like a human birth because animal eyes are round like human eyes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says a woman who miscarries an animal-shaped fetus keeps the birth rules. רבי יוחנן says this is because these creatures have round eyes like people. That means round eyes are normal for animals, so how can אילא call a round eye a blemish?

keyTerms.meaning: She keeps the days of impurity and purity for a boy

steps.confusionAlert: The topic of נדה is not the main point here. The only reason the גמרא brings it is רבי יוחנן's remark that animal eyes are round like human eyes.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction: A woman who miscarries a type of domestic animal,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in נדה 21a.

phrases.english: or wild animal, or bird,
whether non-kosher or kosher,
if it is male, she observes the days for a male.
If it is female, she observes the days for a female,
if it is unknown, she observes the days for a male and for a female,
this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rabba bar bar Ḥana said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Meir?

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְגַלְגַּל עֵינוֹ עָגוֹל כְּשֶׁל אָדָם!
phrases.english: Since its eyeball is round like that of a person!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the idea from step 29 that round eyes are not normal for animals.
steps.kashyaTarget: אילא's blemish of an eye that is round like a person's.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן says animals normally have round, human-like eyes. Something normal cannot be a blemish.

steps.title: Black part versus white part of the eye
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that the two sources are talking about different parts of the eye: one about the black part, the other about the white part.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: It is not a problem. This one is about the black part, and that one is about the white part.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the contradiction. The two sources are talking about different parts of the eye.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being round 'like a person's' can mean the black part of the eye or the white part. One source is about the black part and the other is about the white part, so both statements can be true. The משנה's blemish and רבי מאיר's reason do not really clash.

keyTerms.meaning: The black part of the eye
The white part of the eye

steps.whatToRemember: A round eye can be a blemish in one part of the eye and normal in another part. That is how both sources can be true.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
It is not difficult;
this is about the black part, and that is about the white part.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the two sources into different cases (black part versus white part of the eye)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources talk about the same kind of roundness, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each source is about a different part of the eye, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: A pig-like mouth does not need to be pointed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a mouth like a pig's. רב פפא says the upper lip hanging over the lower lip is enough, even if the mouth is not pointed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'Or its mouth looks like a pig's.' רב פפא said: Do not think this only means a mouth that is both pointed and has the upper lip hanging over. Rather, once the upper lip hangs over, it counts, even if the mouth is not pointed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next item on אילא's list, 'its mouth is like a pig's.' רב פפא explains exactly what this means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pig's mouth has two features: it comes to a point, and its upper lip hangs over the lower one. רב פפא says only the second feature is needed. So the blemish is wider than a beginner might think.

keyTerms.meaning: Spread over, the upper lip hanging over the lower lip
Do not say, do not think

phrases.english: Or its mouth is similar to that of a pig.
Rav Pappa says:
Do not say it means only where it is pointed and overlaps,
phrases.notes: 'Overlaps' means the upper lip hangs over the lower lip, like a pig's.

phrases.english: Rather, once it overlaps,
even though it is not pointed, it counts.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֵּימָא דִּשְׁפִיד וּפְרִוס, אֶלָּא כֵּיוָן דִּפְרִוס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the round-eye item to the next item on אילא's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An overhanging upper lip alone is enough to count as a 'pig-like mouth'. The mouth does not need to be pointed.

steps.title: Whose view is 'the speaking part of the tongue'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of losing most of the speaking part of the tongue and asks which תנא holds this view.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'Or most of the speaking part of its tongue was removed.' Whose view is our משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the last item on אילא's list and asks whose opinion it follows. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not say 'most of the tongue.' It says 'most of the speaking part.' That exact wording suggests a specific opinion, so the גמרא wants to know whose it is.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'speaking part' of the tongue, the part matching what a person uses to talk

phrases.english: Or that most of the speaking part of its tongue was removed.
phrases.notes: Another quote from the משנה. 'Speaking part' means the part of the tongue that matches the part a person uses to talk.

phrases.english: Whose opinion is our משנה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next item on אילא's list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that the blemish depends on the 'speaking part' of the tongue.

steps.title: It follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי יהודה, and proves it from a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי יהודה, as a ברייתא teaches: 'And one where most of the tongue was removed.' רבי יהודה says: most of the speaking part of its tongue.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question: the משנה follows רבי יהודה. It brings a ברייתא where רבי יהודה uses this exact wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first gives the plain rule, 'most of the tongue.' רבי יהודה then makes it narrower: what counts is most of the speaking part. Our משנה uses רבי יהודה's wording, so it follows him.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'speaking part of the tongue' wording in the משנה comes from רבי יהודה. The plain view in the ברייתא only speaks of 'most of the tongue.'

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Yehuda,
as it is taught in a ברייתא:
And one where most of the tongue was removed;
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Most of the speaking part of its tongue.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי יהודה. The ברייתא shows that he is the one who measures by the speaking part of the tongue.

steps.title: New משנה: an animal whose lower jaw sticks out
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה tells of a firstborn animal whose lower jaw stuck out past the upper jaw. The חכמים told רבן גמליאל it is a blemish.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a story about an animal whose lower jaw stuck out past the upper jaw. רבן גמליאל asked the חכמים, and they said: this is a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It tells a real story where the חכמים ruled that a lower jaw sticking out past the upper jaw is a blemish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the opposite of the 'pig-like mouth,' where the upper lip hangs over. Here the lower jaw is the one that sticks out. The ruling means a firstborn animal like this may be slaughtered.

keyTerms.meaning: A story, a real event used to show a ruling

phrases.english: MISHNA: And there was an incident where the lower jaw
stuck out beyond the upper jaw,
and Rabban Gamliel asked the Sages,
and they said: This is a blemish.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁהַלְּחִי הַתַּחְתּוֹן עוֹדֵף עַל הָעֶלְיוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of אילא's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lower jaw sticking out past the upper jaw is a blemish.

steps.title: Why does the משנה say 'And there was a story'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what earlier teaching the word 'And' in 'And there was a story' connects to.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: What did the תנא teach before, that he now says 'And there was a story'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the משנה opens with 'And,' as if it is adding to something earlier. It asks what that earlier teaching is, which sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A story is usually told to support or clarify a rule. The word 'And' shows that this story connects to something already taught, but it is not clear what.

phrases.english: GEMARA: What did he teach before
that he teaches: "And there was an incident"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about how the new משנה is worded.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which earlier rule the story in the משנה is meant to support.

steps.title: The story shows the dispute is only about the upper lip
steps.stepSummary: The story connects to the 'pig-like mouth' case. The חכמים disagreed with אילא only when the upper lip sticks out. When the lower jaw sticks out, everyone agrees it is a blemish.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because we learned 'its mouth is like a pig's,' and the חכמים disagreed with אילא. So we say: the חכמים disagreed only where the upper lip hangs over the lower. But where the lower sticks out past the upper, it is a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the story connects to the 'pig-like mouth' item, which the חכמים did not accept from אילא. The story shows the limit of their disagreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים rejected אילא's 'pig-like mouth,' meaning an upper lip that hangs over. One might think they rejected every uneven mouth. The story shows that a lower jaw sticking out is a blemish according to everyone.
steps.whatToRemember: An upper lip hanging over is disputed: אילא says it is a blemish and the חכמים disagree. A lower jaw sticking out past the upper is a blemish according to everyone.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. The dispute is only about the upper lip hanging over. The story is about the opposite case, the lower jaw, where there is no dispute.

phrases.english: Because we learned: "Its mouth is similar to a pig's,"
and the Rabbis disagree with Rabbi Ila,
and so we say:
when the Rabbis disagree with Rabbi Ila,
it is where its upper lip hangs over the lower one;
but where the lower one sticks out past the upper one,
this is a blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 36 by linking the story to the 'pig-like mouth' item.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The story shows that the חכמים disagreed with אילא only about an upper lip hanging over. Everyone agrees that a lower jaw sticking out is a blemish.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a story in a משנה can mark the limit of a dispute. A lower jaw sticking out is a blemish according to everyone.
